_comment: HOW THE BUSES RUN THEIR LINES (ADR-0483; the lines themselves are the road file's "bus_lines", ADR-0481). Read once
by the city sim (city_driving.h busService). No copy in C++: a missing file or a missing number runs no buses, and
headway_minutes      the minutes between one bus and the next at a stop: a line gets as many buses as its round
trip (driving time at the free-flow speed and every stop's wait) divided by this, rounded up;
most_buses_per_line  ...but never more than this many;
dwell_seconds        how long a bus stands at each stop with its doors open;
traffic_factor       a bus's leg from one stop to the next as driven, over the same leg at the free-flow speed (its
route's own time): what the lights, the crossings, the traffic and pulling in at the stop cost
it. Used to size each line's fleet and to time the planner's timetable. MEASURED: 4.03 on
river_town (2026-11-22, its 3 lines, 6 buses, 71 legs in 30 minutes; DrivingCounts::busDriven
capacity             people aboard one bus at most: a full bus leaves the rest at the stop for the next.
Sources: [~] a city bus every 6-10 minutes is a frequent service (TCRP Report 165, Transit Capacity and Quality of
Service Manual, 3rd ed., level of service A-B by headway); 15-30 s at a stop is a common dwell for a few riders
(same manual, chapter 6); about 60 aboard a 12 m city bus, 35 seated and the rest standing (same manual, chapter 6).
Guesses to tune by watching, but for the traffic factor, which is measured.
